edition.locus: On the Apparel of Women Book I
edition.witness_note: Single locked witness in repo; second witness not yet locked.

source_text: Si tanta in terris moraretur fides, quanta merces ejus exspectatur in coelis, nulla omnino vestrum, sorores dilectissimae, ex quo Deum vivum cognovisset, et de sua, id est de foeminae conditione didicisset, laetiorem habitum, ne dicam gloriosiorem appetiisset, ut non magis in sordibus ageret, et squalorem potius affectaret, ipsam se circumferens Evam lugentem et poenitentem; quo plenius id quod de Eva trahit (ignominiam dico primi delicti, et invidiam perditionis humanae) omni satisfactionis habitu expiaret. In doloribus et anxietatibus paries, mulier, et ad virum tuum conversio tua; et ille dominabitur tui; et Evam te esse nescis? Vivit sententia Dei super sexum istum, in hoc saeculo: vivat et reatus necesse est. Tu es diaboli janua, tu es arboris illius resignatrix, tu es divinae legis prima desertrix, tu es quae eum persuasisti, quem diabolus aggredi non valuit. Tu imaginem Dei, hominem, tam facile elisisti: propter tuum meritum, id est mortem, etiam Filius Dei mori habuit; et adornari tibi in mente est super pelliceas tuas tunicas? Age nunc, si ab initio rerum et Milesii oves tonderent, et Seres arbores nerent, et Tyrii tinguerent, et Phryges insuerent, et Babylonii intexerent, et margaritae canderent et ceraunia coruscarent, si ipsum quoque aurum jam de terra cum cupiditate prodisset; si jam et speculo tantum mentiri liceret: et haec Eva concupisset de paradiso expulsa, jam mortua, opinor. Ergo nec nunc appetere debet, aut nosse, si cupit reviviscere, quae nec habuerat, nec noverat, quando vivebat. Ideo omnia ista damnatae et mortuae mulieris impedimenta sunt, quasi ad pompam funeris constituta. Nam et illi qui ea constituerunt, damnati in poenam mortis deputantur: illi scilicet angeli, qui ad filias hominum de coelo ruerunt, ut haec quoque ignominia foeminae accedat. Nam cum et materias quasdam bene occultas, et artes plerasque non bene revelatas, saeculo multo magis imperito prodidissent (siquidem et metallorum opera nudaverant, et herbarum ingenia traduxerant, et incantationum vires provulgaverant, et omnem curiositatem, usque ad stellarum interpretationem, designaverant) proprie et quasi peculiariter foeminis instrumentum istud muliebris gloriae contulerunt: lumina lapillorum quibus monilia variantur: et circulos ex auro, quibus brachia arctantur: et medicamenta ex fuco, quibus lanae colorantur: et illum ipsum nigrum pulverem, quo oculorum exordia producuntur. Haec qualia sint, interim jam ex doctorum suorum qualitate et conditione pronuntiari potest, quod nihil ad integritatem peccatores, nihil ad castitatem adamatores, nihil ad timorem Dei desertores spiritus, aut monstrare potuerunt aut praestare. Si doctrinae dicendae sunt, mali magistri male docuerint necesse est. Si mercedes pro libidine, nullius rei turpis merces decora est. Quid autem tanti fuit ista monstrare sicut conferre? utrumne mulieres, sine materiis splendoris, et sine ingeniis decoris, placere non possent hominibus, quae adhuc incultae et incompositae et (ut ita dixerim) crudae ac rudes, angelos moverant? Anne sordidi, et per gratuitum usum contumeliosi amatores viderentur, si nihil foeminis in connubium allectis contulissent? Sed haec non capit aestimare, nihil plus desiderare poterant, quae angelos possidebant, magno scilicet nupserant. Enimvero, qui utique interdum cogitabant unde cecidissent, et post libidinum vaporata momenta coelum suspirabant, illud ipsum bonum foeminarum naturalis decoris, ut caussam mali, sic remuneraverunt, ne eis profuisset felicitas sua, sed ut devectum de simplicitate et sinceritate una cum ipsis in offensam Dei pervenirent. Certi erant omnem, et gloriam, et ambitionem, et affectationem per carnem placendi Deo displicere. Hi sunt nempe angeli quos judicaturi sumus, hi sunt angeli quibus in lavacro renuntiamus; haec sunt utique, per quae ab homine judicari meruerunt. Quid ergo facient apud judices suos res eorum? quod est commercium damnaturis cum damnandis? Opinor, quod Christo et Beliae. Qua constantia tribunal illud ascendimus, decreturi adversus eos, quorum munera appetimus? Nam et vobis eadem tunc substantia angelica repromissa, idem sexus qui et viris, eamdem judicandi dignationem pollicetur: nisi ergo hic jam praejudicaverimus, res eorum praedamnando, quas in illis tunc damnaturi sumus, illi potius nos judicabunt atque damnabunt. Scio scripturam Enoch, quae hunc ordinem angelis dedit, non recipi a quibusdam, quia nec in armarium judaicum admittitur. Opinor, non putaverunt illam ante cataclysmum editam, post eum casum orbis, omnium rerum abolitorem, salvam esse potuisse. Si ista ratio est, recordentur pronepotem ipsius Enoch fuisse superstitem cataclysmi Noë, qui utique domestico nomine et haereditaria traditione audierat et meminerat, de proavi sui penes Deum gratia, et de omnibus praedicatis ejus; cum Enoch filio suo Mathusalae nihil aliud mandaverit, quam ut notitiam eorum posteris suis traderet. Igitur sine dubio potuit Noë, in praedicationis delegatione successisse, vel quia et alias non tacuisset tam de Dei conservatoris sui dispositione, quam de ipsa domus suae gloria. Hoc si non tam expedite haberet, illud quoque assertionem scripturae illius tueretur. Perinde potuit abolefactam eam violentia cataclysmi, in spiritu rursus reformare: quemadmodum et Hierosolymis Babylonia expugnatione deletis, omne instrumentum judaicae litteraturae per Esdram constat restauratum. Sed cum Enoch eadem scriptura etiam de Domino praedicarit, a nobis quidem nihil omnino rejiciendum est, quod pertinet ad nos. Et legimus, omnem Scripturam aedificationi habilem divinitus inspirari. A Judaeis potest jam videri propterea rejecta, sicut et caetera fere quae Christum sonant. Nec utique mirum hoc, si scripturas aliquas non receperunt de eo locutas, quem et ipsum coram loquentem non erant recepturi. Eo accedit, quod Enoch apud Judam Apostolum testimonium possidet. Nulla nunc muliebri pompae nota inusta sit praedamnationis, de exitu auctorum. Nihil angelis illis imputetur, praeter repudium coeli, et matrimonium carnis. Rerum ipsarum qualitates examinemus, ut consilia quoque concupiscentiae earum deprehendamus. Habitus foeminae duplicem speciem circumfert, cultum, ornatum. Cultum dicimus, quem mundum muliebrem vocant; ornatum, quem immundum muliebrem convenit dici. Ille in auro, et argento, et gemmis, et vestibus deputatur: ista in cura capilli, et cutis, et earum partium corporis, quae oculos trahunt. Alteri ambitionis crimen intendimus, alteri prostitutionis: ut jam hinc prospicias, Dei ancilla, quid ex his disciplinae tuae conveniat, quae de diversis institutis censearis, scilicet humilitatis et castitatis.
pass_a_gloss: If so much faith would remain on earth, as great a reward of it is expected in heaven, none of you, most beloved sisters, from the time that you would have known the living God, and would have learned about your own, that is, the female condition, would have desired a more joyful, or rather, a more glorious appearance, so that you would not be more in filth, and would rather affect squalor, carrying around with you the mourning and repentant Eve; by which the more fully that which you draw from Eve (I say the ignominy of the first sin, and the envy of human perdition) you would expiate with every habit of satisfaction. In pains and anxieties, you will bring forth, woman, and your turning will be to your husband, and he will dominate you; and you do not know that you are Eve? The sentence of God lives on over this sex, in this world: and the guilt must live. You are the gate of the devil, you are the transgressor of that tree, you are the first deserter of the divine law, you are the one who persuaded him, whom the devil was not able to attack. You so easily destroyed the image of God, man: on account of your merit, that is, death, even the Son of God had to die; and it is in your mind to adorn yourself in your mind beyond your woolen tunics? Come now, if from the beginning of things, the Milesians sheared sheep, and the Seres wove trees, and the Tyrians dyed, and the Phrygians sewed, and the Babylonians intertwined, and pearls shone and corals sparkled, if even gold itself, already with desire, would come forth from the earth; if already it would be allowed to lie so much with a mirror: and these things Eve, expelled from paradise, already dead, would have desired, I think. Therefore, neither now should she desire, nor know, if she wishes to revive, what she neither had nor knew when she was alive. For this reason, all these things are the impediments of a condemned and dead woman, as if established for the pomp of a funeral. For also those who established these things are assigned to the punishment of death: those angels, namely, who rushed from heaven to the daughters of men, so that this ignominy also would be added to the woman. For when they had revealed certain well-hidden materials, and many arts not well revealed, to a much more ignorant world (since they had also uncovered the works of metals, and had handed over the ingenuities of herbs, and had made public the powers of incantations, and had designated all curiosity, up to the interpretation of stars), they properly and as if peculiarly conferred this instrument of female glory upon women: the lights of stones with which necklaces are varied, and the circles of gold with which arms are bound, and the medications from dye with which wool is colored, and that very black powder with which the beginnings of the eyes are produced. What kind these things are can already be declared from the quality and condition of their teachers, that they were able to show or provide nothing for integrity, nothing for chastity, nothing for the fear of God, but only for sinners, lovers, and deserters of the spirit. If they are to be called teachings, evil teachers must have taught evil. If rewards for lust, the reward of no shameful thing is decorous. What was the purpose of showing these things, as if to confer them? Was it that women, without materials of splendor and without ingenuities of decoration, could not please men, who, still uncultivated and uncomposed and (so to speak) crude and rude, had moved angels? Or did they seem to be sordid and contemptuous lovers, if they had conferred nothing upon women, who had been allured into marriage? But this does not allow for estimation, they could desire nothing more, who possessed angels, having married, of course, with great pomp. Indeed, those who at some time thought about whence they had fallen, and after the fleeting moments of lust, sighed for heaven, rewarded that very good of women, the natural decoration, as the cause of evil, so that their own happiness would not have profited them, but so that, having been diverted from simplicity and sincerity, they would come together with them into the offense of God. They were certain that all glory, and ambition, and affectation of pleasing God through the flesh was displeasing to God. These are, of course, the angels whom we will judge, these are the angels to whom we renounce in baptism; these are the things, of course, by which they deserved to be judged by men. What, therefore, will their things do before their judges? What is the commerce of the damned with those who are to be damned? I think it is the same as with Christ and Belial. With what consistency do we ascend to that tribunal, to decree against those whose gifts we desire? For also to you, the same angelic substance is promised, the same sex which is also for men, the same dignity of judging is promised: unless, therefore, we have already pre-judged here, by condemning their things, which we will damn in them, then they will rather judge and condemn us. I know that the scripture of Enoch, which gave this order to angels, is not received by some, because it is not admitted into the Jewish archive. I think they did not consider it to have been edited before the flood, and to have been preserved after the destruction of the world, the destroyer of all things. If this is the reason, let them remember that Noah, the great-grandson of Enoch, was a survivor of the flood, who, of course, had heard and remembered from his domestic name and hereditary tradition, about the favor of his great-grandfather with God, and about all his predictions; since Enoch had entrusted nothing else to his son Methuselah, than that he should hand down the knowledge of these things to his posterity. Therefore, without doubt, Noah could have succeeded in the delegation of preaching, or because he had not been silent about the disposition of God, his preserver, and about the glory of his own house. If this is not so readily available, that assertion of scripture would also defend it. In the same way, it could have been re-formed in spirit, after having been destroyed by the violence of the flood: just as also in Jerusalem, after the Babylonian conquest, all the instruments of Jewish literature were restored through Ezra. But since Enoch, in the same scripture, also predicted the Lord, we, of course, reject nothing that pertains to us. And we read that all scripture is divinely inspired for edification. It can now be seen by the Jews to have been rejected for this reason, just as almost all the things that speak of Christ. Nor is it surprising, if they did not receive certain scriptures that spoke of him, whom they themselves were not about to receive, speaking in person. It is added that Enoch has testimony with the apostle Jude. Let no mark of condemnation be imposed upon female pomp, from the outcome of its authors. Let nothing be imputed to those angels, except the repudiation of heaven, and marriage to the flesh. Let us examine the qualities of the things themselves, so that we may also understand the counsels of their desires. The habit of a woman carries a double species, cultivation, and ornament. We call cultivation that which they call the worldly woman; ornament, that which is suited to be called the impure woman. The former is assigned to gold, and silver, and gems, and clothes: the latter, to the care of hair, and skin, and those parts of the body which attract the eyes. We charge the former with the crime of ambition, the latter with the crime of prostitution: so that already from this, you may look ahead, handmaid of God, what of these things is suitable for your discipline, who are judged to be from diverse institutions, namely, of humility and chastity.

pass_b_english: If the faith on earth matched the reward expected in heaven, not one of you, beloved sisters, would have wanted a more joyful — let alone glorious — appearance after knowing the living God and learning your own condition as women. You would rather have chosen filth and squalor, dragging around a mourning, repentant Eve, so as to fully atone for what you inherited from her: the ignominy of the first sin and the envy of human perdition. "In pain and anxiety you will bear children, woman, and your desire will be for your husband, and he will rule over you" (Genesis 3:16). Do you not know you are Eve? God's sentence still stands over this sex in this age, and the guilt must remain. You are the devil's gateway, the one who unsealed that tree, the first deserter of divine law, the one who persuaded the man the devil could not attack. You so easily destroyed God's image, man; because of your merit — death — even the Son of God had to die. And you still think to adorn yourself beyond your woolen tunics? Come now: even if from the beginning the Milesians sheared sheep, the Seres wove silk, the Tyrians dyed, the Phrygians sewed, the Babylonians embroidered, pearls gleamed and corals sparkled, gold itself came up from the earth with desire, and mirrors were allowed to lie — Eve, expelled from paradise and already dead, would have craved these things, I think. So she should neither desire nor know them now, if she wants to live again, since she neither had nor knew them when she was alive. All these things are the impediments of a condemned, dead woman, set up like funeral pomp. Those who invented them are likewise sentenced to death: the angels who plunged from heaven to the daughters of men, adding this disgrace to women. They revealed hidden materials and obscure arts to an ignorant world — metalworking, herbal lore, incantations, even astrology — and specifically gave women the tools of female vanity: gemstones for necklaces, gold bands for arms, dyes for wool, black powder to outline the eyes. The quality of these things is already declared by the character of their teachers: they offered nothing for integrity, nothing for chastity, nothing for the fear of God — only for sinners, lovers, deserters of the Spirit. If these are teachings, evil teachers taught evil. If they are rewards for lust, no shameful reward is honorable. What was the point of displaying these things as gifts? Could women not please men without splendor and artifice — the same crude, unrefined women who moved angels? Or would the angels have seemed sordid, insulting lovers, if they gave nothing to the women they seduced into marriage? But that calculation fails: they could desire nothing more, since they possessed angels and had married in high style. Indeed, those angels who sometimes remembered their fall and sighed for heaven after their fleeting lust rewarded women's natural beauty — the very cause of evil — so that their own happiness would not benefit them, but they would be dragged down from simplicity and sincerity into offense against God. They knew full well that all glory, ambition, and affectation of pleasing God through the flesh displeases God. These are the angels we will judge; these are the angels we renounce in baptism; these are the things by which they deserved to be judged by men. What will their gifts do before their judges? What commerce can the damned have with the damned? I say it is like Christ and Belial. With what consistency do we ascend that tribunal to condemn those whose gifts we crave? The same angelic substance is promised to you, the same sex as men, the same dignity of judging — unless we have already prejudged the matter here by condemning their things, which we will later damn in them; then they will judge and condemn us. I know the Book of Enoch, which assigned this order to angels, is rejected by some because it is not in the Jewish canon. They think it could not have survived the flood, the destroyer of all things. If so, let them remember Noah, Enoch's great-grandson, survived the flood and heard by family tradition of his ancestor's favor with God and all his prophecies; Enoch charged his son Methuselah to pass this knowledge down. Noah could certainly have succeeded in his preaching mission, since he spoke of God who preserved him and of his own house's glory. Even if that record was lost, the flood's violence could not destroy what the Spirit can reform — just as Ezra restored all Jewish literature after Babylon destroyed Jerusalem. Since Enoch also prophesied the Lord in that same scripture, we reject nothing that pertains to us. We read that all Scripture is divinely inspired for edification. The Jews reject it for the same reason they reject nearly everything that speaks of Christ — no surprise, since they would not receive him speaking in person. Moreover, Enoch has the testimony of the apostle Jude. Let no mark of condemnation stain female pomp because of its authors' fate. Charge those angels only with rejecting heaven and marrying flesh. Let us examine the things themselves, to uncover the desires behind them. A woman's appearance has two forms: cultivation and ornament. Cultivation is what they call the worldly woman — gold, silver, gems, clothing. Ornament is what befits the impure woman — care of hair, skin, and those body parts that draw the eye. We charge the first with ambition, the second with prostitution. So look ahead, handmaid of God, and see which of these suits your discipline, you who are judged by a different standard: humility and chastity.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the complex conditional moods and theological nuances of the Latin text. Scripture citations (Genesis 3:16) are correctly identified and applied to the relevant clauses. Pass A and Pass B are consistent with the Locked Latin.
